newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse closes weekly trading higher.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse closes weekly trading higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed its weekly trading on Friday higher, registering its best performance so far this year, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 476.55 points from 466.28 last Friday.
"The index recorded its highest performance since the beginning of the year, up 6.58 percent," Mohamed Mekouar, analyst at Upline Securities, told Reuters.
The Friday session witnessed a surge of blue chip stocks including Wafabank, Mekouar said.
Wafabank gained 25 dirhams in one week to close at 595 dirhams on Friday.
Ciments de l'Oriental, the second largest cement firm and the most liquid stock in the sector, recorded an 18.2 percent increase since the beginning of the year, Mekouar said.

In 1996, the cement volume for the whole sector increased by 2.6 percent compared to 1995. The best performances were recorded by Ciments de l'Oriental (4.46 percent) followed by another listed firm, Asmar (4.11 percent).
"Despite the highly positive result for 1996, the CIOR closing price which stands at 475 dirhams is expensive," Mekouar added.
Mekouar said he shared what he called a common point of view of market analysts who were concerned about what they saw as "the overvaluation" of many stock shares.
CIOR rose 25 dirhams in one week to close at 475.
ONA group, the country's largest private group, rose 20 dirhams to close at 590.
Morocco's second largest conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement remained stable at 565 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 34.6 million dirhams compared with 25.6 million dirhams last Friday.
